question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 24.02(1)(a), which of the following would be classified as an "adverse fact" regarding a property?
choice_a: A cosmetic paint color that a buyer personally dislikes
choice_b: The seller's opinion that the neighborhood is not as quiet as it used to be
choice_c: A licensee's personal preference for a different floor plan
choice_d: A condition that a competent licensee recognizes as significantly reducing the structural integrity of an improvement to the real estate
explanation: REEB 24.02(1)(a) defines "adverse fact" to include a condition or occurrence that a competent licensee recognizes as significantly and adversely affecting the property's value, significantly reducing the structural integrity of improvements, or presenting a significant health risk to occupants.

question: Under REEB 24.02(1)(b), an "adverse fact" also includes information indicating what?
choice_a: That a party to a transaction is unable to perform, or does not intend to perform, an obligation under a contract or agreement related to the transaction
choice_b: That a party is a first-time buyer
choice_c: That a party is represented by an attorney
choice_d: That a party lives out of state
explanation: REEB 24.02(1)(b) extends the definition of "adverse fact" to information indicating that a party cannot or does not intend to meet an obligation under a transaction contract or agreement.

question: How does a "material adverse fact" differ from an "adverse fact" under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 24.02?
choice_a: A material adverse fact only applies to commercial property, while an adverse fact applies only to residential property
choice_b: A material adverse fact is an adverse fact that a party has indicated is of significance to them, or one generally recognized by a competent licensee as significant to a reasonable party in deciding whether to enter into or complete a transaction
choice_c: A material adverse fact must be recorded with the county register of deeds before closing
choice_d: There is no legal distinction; the two terms are interchangeable under Wisconsin law
explanation: REEB 24.02(12) defines "material adverse fact" as an adverse fact that a party indicates is of significance, or one generally recognized by a competent licensee as significant to a reasonable party, in deciding whether to enter into or complete a transaction.

question: Under REEB 24.02(19), a "written proposal" includes which of the following?
choice_a: Only the final, fully executed offer to purchase
choice_b: Verbal counteroffers communicated by telephone
choice_c: A written counteroffer, amendment, or notice exchanged between parties during a transaction
choice_d: Marketing brochures prepared by the listing firm
explanation: REEB 24.02(19) defines "written proposal" broadly to include any written document provided by one party to another during a transaction, including notices, offers, counteroffers, options, exchanges, rental agreements, and amendments.

question: Which of the following would meet the definition of a "qualified third party" under REEB 24.02(14), whose written inspection report a licensee may rely on?
choice_a: Any friend or relative of the buyer who has looked at the property
choice_b: The listing licensee performing a walk-through of the home
choice_c: The seller, regardless of qualifications
choice_d: A person reasonably believed by the licensee to have the expertise necessary to meet industry standards for the type of inspection or investigation performed
explanation: REEB 24.02(14) defines "qualified third party" as a federal, state, or local governmental agency, or a person the licensee reasonably believes has expertise meeting industry standards for the inspection or investigation performed, consistent with Wis. Stat. § 452.23(2)(b).

question: Under REEB 24.02(7), two corporations are considered "commonly controlled" for purposes of the tie-in arrangement exception when:
choice_a: The same persons own at least 80% of the combined voting power and at least 80% of the total value of shares of each corporation
choice_b: They share the same registered agent in Wisconsin
choice_c: They have at least one common officer
choice_d: They are located in the same county
explanation: REEB 24.02(7) defines "commonly controlled corporation" using an 80%/80% common-ownership test, which becomes relevant to the builder tie-in exception in REEB 24.075(3)(b).

question: How does REEB 24.02(16m) define a "right of first refusal"?
choice_a: The right of a buyer to rescind an accepted offer within 24 hours
choice_b: The right of a person to have the first opportunity to purchase or lease the real property in question
choice_c: The right of a seller to reject any offer below the listing price
choice_d: The right of a licensee to refuse to submit an offer to purchase
explanation: REEB 24.02(16m) defines "right of first refusal" as the right of a person to have the first opportunity to purchase or lease the real property in question.

question: REEB 24.03(1) prohibits licensees from discriminating against or denying equal services to any person on a basis prohibited by fair housing law, referencing which statutory chapter?
choice_a: Wis. Stat. ch. 700, governing property
choice_b: Wis. Stat. ch. 706, governing conveyances
choice_c: Wis. Stat. ch. 106, subchapter II (Wisconsin's open housing law), along with the 1988 amendments to the federal Fair Housing Act
choice_d: Wis. Stat. ch. 452, subchapter I only
explanation: REEB 24.03(1) requires licensees to comply with fair housing standards, referencing the 1988 amendments to the federal Fair Housing Act and Wis. Stat. ch. 106, subch. II.

question: Under REEB 24.03(2)(a), if a licensee is asked to perform a service beyond their competence, what must the licensee do to comply with the rule?
choice_a: Decline the listing entirely and refer the client to a different firm
choice_b: Proceed with the work and disclose the limitation only if asked
choice_c: Charge a reduced commission to reflect the limitation
choice_d: Engage a person who is competent to provide the necessary assistance, identify that person, and document their contribution in the transaction records
explanation: REEB 24.03(2)(a) provides that a licensee shall not render services beyond their competence unless assistance is obtained from a person competent to perform those aspects, with that person identified and their contribution documented in the transaction records.

question: Under REEB 24.03(2)(d), a licensee performing a required property inspection is NOT expected to possess the technical expertise of which of the following?
choice_a: A home inspector, plumber, electrician, or land surveyor
choice_b: A licensed real estate broker
choice_c: A licensed appraiser employed by the same firm
choice_d: The Wisconsin Real Estate Examining Board
explanation: REEB 24.03(2)(d) clarifies that a licensee need not have the technical expertise of specialized professionals such as home inspectors, plumbers, electricians, or surveyors.

question: What does Wis. Stat. § 452.136(1) require regarding a licensee's advertising, as incorporated into the conduct rules by REEB 24.04?
choice_a: A licensee must include the seller's name in every advertisement
choice_b: A licensee may not advertise in a manner that is false, deceptive, or misleading
choice_c: A licensee may advertise a property at any price they choose, regardless of the listing agreement
choice_d: A licensee must obtain board pre-approval before publishing any advertisement
explanation: Wis. Stat. § 452.136(1), which REEB 24.04 incorporates by reference as a licensee conduct standard, prohibits false, deceptive, or misleading advertising.
source_note: Wis. Stat. § 452.136(1); Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 24.04

question: Under Wis. Stat. § 452.136(2)(a), what must a licensee's advertisement of brokerage services generally disclose?
choice_a: The licensee's home address
choice_b: The exact commission rate being charged
choice_c: The name of the firm, as licensed or filed with the department, disclosed in a manner that clearly indicates the firm is a business entity rather than a private party
choice_d: The firm's federal employer identification number
explanation: Wis. Stat. § 452.136(2)(a) requires advertising to disclose the firm's licensed or filed name in a way that clearly indicates it is a business entity, with a limited exception for rental advertisements of licensee-owned property.

question: Under Wis. Stat. § 452.136(3), when may a firm advertise a specific property for sale?
choice_a: Any time the property is publicly for sale, regardless of who holds the listing
choice_b: Only after the property has been under contract for at least 30 days
choice_c: Only with verbal permission from the seller
choice_d: Only if the firm holds the listing on the property or has obtained written consent from the firm that holds the listing
explanation: Wis. Stat. § 452.136(3) prohibits a firm from advertising real estate unless the firm holds the listing or has obtained the listing firm's written consent.

question: Under Wis. Stat. § 452.136(4), a licensee may advertise a property at a price other than the price agreed to with the owner only if:
choice_a: The advertisement uses a price range or general terms that still accurately reflect the actual agreed-upon price
choice_b: The licensee believes the market supports a higher price
choice_c: The seller has been unreachable for more than 10 days
choice_d: The licensee has already received a competing written offer
explanation: Wis. Stat. § 452.136(4) generally bars advertising a property at a price other than the one agreed to with the owner, except that a range or general terms may be used if they still accurately reflect the actual agreed price.

question: Under REEB 24.05(4), when may a listing firm pay compensation or an incentive to a licensee who is acting as a buyer in the same transaction?
choice_a: At any time, without any disclosure obligation
choice_b: Only after obtaining the prior written consent of the seller
choice_c: Only if the buyer-licensee waives their own commission
choice_d: Only if the transaction closes within 60 days
explanation: REEB 24.05(4) prohibits a listing firm from paying compensation or an incentive to a licensee acting as a buyer in a transaction without the seller's prior written consent.

question: Under REEB 24.05(5), a licensee who intends to act as a principal (rather than as an agent) in a transaction must disclose that fact and their license status in writing no later than which of the following?
choice_a: At the closing table, immediately before signing
choice_b: Only if directly asked by the other party
choice_c: The earliest of first substantive contact exchanging transaction information, a showing of the property, or any negotiation with the seller or their representative
choice_d: Within 30 days after the offer is accepted
explanation: REEB 24.05(5)(a)-(b) requires a licensee acting as a principal to disclose their license status and intent in writing at the earliest of initial contact exchanging transaction information, a showing, or any negotiation with the seller, listing firm, or representing party.

question: Under REEB 24.07(1)(b), what must a listing firm do before entering into a listing contract for improved property?
choice_a: Obtain a third-party home inspection report at the firm's expense
choice_b: Require the seller to complete a certified appraisal
choice_c: Confirm the property is free of any liens
choice_d: Inspect the accessible areas of the property and inquire of the seller about the condition of the structure, mechanical systems, and other relevant aspects
explanation: REEB 24.07(1)(b) requires a listing firm to inspect the property's accessible areas and inquire of the seller about the condition of the structure and mechanical systems before executing a listing contract.

question: Under REEB 24.07(1)(d), a licensee's required property inspection does NOT obligate the licensee to do which of the following?
choice_a: Operate mechanical equipment, open panels or covers, move furniture, or access areas reachable only by ladder or crawling
choice_b: Walk through each room of the home that is freely accessible
choice_c: Note a visibly missing handrail on an interior stairway
choice_d: Inquire about the age of the roof if visibly relevant
explanation: REEB 24.07(1)(d) limits the scope of required inspections: licensees need not operate mechanical equipment, open panels/covers, move furniture, or access areas presenting unreasonable injury risk or reachable only by ladder or crawling.

question: Under REEB 24.07(2), when must a licensee disclose a known material adverse fact to a party in a transaction?
choice_a: Only if the party specifically asks about that exact issue
choice_b: In writing and in a timely fashion, unless the licensee is legally prohibited from disclosing it
choice_c: Only after the offer to purchase has been accepted
choice_d: Verbally is sufficient; no writing is required
explanation: REEB 24.07(2) requires licensees to disclose known material adverse facts to each party in writing and in a timely fashion, unless disclosure is otherwise prohibited by law.

question: Under REEB 24.07(6), if a licensee's own inspection reveals information materially inconsistent with the seller's statements or a third-party inspection report, what must the licensee do?
choice_a: Keep the discrepancy confidential to avoid disrupting the transaction
choice_b: Resolve the discrepancy personally before disclosing anything
choice_c: Disclose the inconsistency in writing and in a timely manner to the parties
choice_d: Report the discrepancy only to the board, not the parties
explanation: REEB 24.07(6) requires licensees to disclose, in writing and in a timely manner to the parties, material inconsistencies between their own inspection findings and a seller's statements or a third-party report.

question: What does REEB 24.07(7) prohibit?
choice_a: Referring a client to another licensee for a second opinion
choice_b: Discussing comparable sales data with a cooperating broker
choice_c: Declining to personally show a competitor's listing
choice_d: Knowingly giving false information about another licensee or about property listed with another licensee
explanation: REEB 24.07(7) provides that licensees shall not knowingly give false information about another licensee or about property listed with another licensee.

question: Under REEB 24.075(1), a licensee may NOT condition the sale of real estate they own or effectively control upon which of the following?
choice_a: The buyer's agreement to also purchase another, separate parcel of real estate
choice_b: The buyer's ability to obtain financing
choice_c: The buyer completing a standard home inspection
choice_d: The buyer signing a lead-paint disclosure form
explanation: REEB 24.075(1) prohibits a licensee from conditioning the sale of real estate they own or effectively control on the buyer agreeing to purchase another, separate parcel.

question: REEB 24.075(2) also prohibits a licensee from conditioning the sale of real estate on the buyer agreeing to do what?
choice_a: Use the licensee's preferred title company
choice_b: List the real estate being purchased, or other real estate the buyer owns, with the licensee
choice_c: Close within 45 days
choice_d: Sign a buyer agency agreement covering future purchases
explanation: REEB 24.075(2) forbids a licensee from conditioning a property sale on the buyer agreeing to list the property being purchased, or other real estate the buyer owns, with that licensee.

question: Under REEB 24.075(3), a licensee may generally not condition the sale of vacant land on the buyer's agreement to use a particular builder for improvements. Which of the following is a recognized exception to that rule?
choice_a: The builder is a personal friend of the licensee
choice_b: The builder offers the licensee a referral fee
choice_c: The builder and the licensee are the same entity, or are commonly controlled corporations whose business involves selling improved property, provided the relationship is fully disclosed
choice_d: The buyer has not yet selected any builder
explanation: REEB 24.075(3)(b) recognizes an exception where the builder and licensee are the same entity or commonly controlled corporations engaged in the business of selling improved property, so long as this relationship is fully disclosed.

question: Under REEB 24.08, which of the following must a licensee put in writing to express the exact agreement of the parties?
choice_a: Only listing contracts exceeding $500,000 in value
choice_b: Only agreements involving commercial property
choice_c: Only agreements where the parties are not represented by attorneys
choice_d: Listing contracts, buyer agency agreements, offers to purchase, property management agreements, options, and other written proposals regarding transactions
explanation: REEB 24.08 requires licensees to put in writing all listing contracts, guaranteed sales agreements, buyer agency agreements, offers to purchase, property management agreements, options, financial obligations, and other written proposals expressing the exact agreement of the parties.

question: Under REEB 24.08, when is a licensee excused from the requirement to put a transaction agreement in writing?
choice_a: When the writing is completed by the parties or their attorneys, or the writing is outside the scope of the licensee's authority under ch. REEB 16
choice_b: Whenever the transaction value is under $50,000
choice_c: Whenever both parties are represented by the same firm
choice_d: There is no exception; every agreement must always be drafted by the licensee
explanation: REEB 24.08 provides that the writing requirement does not apply if the writing is completed by the parties or their attorneys, or if it is outside the scope of the licensee's authority under ch. REEB 16.

question: Under REEB 24.09, a licensee attempting to secure a listing or buyer agency agreement may NOT do which of the following?
choice_a: Provide a comparative market analysis to support a suggested listing price
choice_b: Mislead a potential client about the benefits of using the licensee's services, or about the market value of the real estate or business opportunity
choice_c: Explain the services included in a buyer agency agreement
choice_d: Decline to represent a buyer outside the licensee's normal service area
explanation: REEB 24.09 prohibits licensees from misleading a potential client regarding the benefits of using the licensee's services, or regarding the market value of real estate or a business opportunity to be handled under an agency agreement.

question: What is a "net listing," which is prohibited under REEB 24.10?
choice_a: A listing contract with no expiration date
choice_b: A listing contract that sets the commission at a flat percentage of the sale price
choice_c: A listing contract that guarantees the owner a stipulated net price, with the firm keeping any amount received above that price as its commission
choice_d: A listing contract that allows the seller to cancel at any time
explanation: REEB 24.10 prohibits licensees from obtaining or negotiating a listing contract that provides the owner a stipulated net price, with any excess over that price going to the firm as commission.

question: Under REEB 24.12(1), may a licensee disclose the specific terms of one prospective buyer's offer to purchase to other prospective buyers?
choice_a: Yes, disclosure of specific offer terms to other buyers is always required
choice_b: Yes, but only if the seller has already rejected the offer
choice_c: No, unless the buyer submitting the offer is a licensee themselves
choice_d: No, except as provided under the right-of-first-refusal exception; the licensee should instead encourage all buyers to submit their best offer
explanation: REEB 24.12(1) generally prohibits disclosing the terms of one prospective buyer's offer to other prospective buyers, instead directing licensees to encourage all buyers to submit their best offers, subject to the right-of-first-refusal exception in sub. (2).

question: Under REEB 24.12(2), when a property is subject to a known right of first refusal, what must the licensee do?
choice_a: Disclose the right of first refusal in writing and in a timely manner to persons seeking to acquire an interest subject to that right
choice_b: Automatically void any offer submitted by a buyer other than the rights-holder
choice_c: Refuse to accept offers until the rights-holder responds
choice_d: Keep the existence of the right confidential to avoid discouraging other buyers
explanation: REEB 24.12(2) requires a licensee who knows a property is subject to a right of first refusal to disclose that right in writing and in a timely manner to persons seeking to acquire an interest in the property.

question: Under REEB 24.13(1), when may a licensee refuse to draft or submit a written proposal on behalf of a party?
choice_a: Whenever the licensee personally believes the offer price is too low
choice_b: Only when the terms of the proposal would be contrary to the other party's specific written instructions
choice_c: Whenever the proposal includes a financing contingency
choice_d: Whenever the buyer is not pre-approved for financing
explanation: REEB 24.13(1) prohibits a licensee from refusing to draft or submit a written proposal unless its terms are contrary to the other party's specific written instructions.

question: Under REEB 24.13(2), a listing firm must permit access to a listed property for showing purposes to buyers and those assisting them:
choice_a: Only during standard business hours, Monday through Friday
choice_b: Only if the buyer is already pre-approved for a mortgage
choice_c: Without unreasonable delay, unless the access is contrary to the seller's specific written instructions
choice_d: Only after a written offer has been submitted
explanation: REEB 24.13(2) requires listing firms to permit access to a listed property for showing purposes without unreasonable delay, unless access is contrary to the seller's specific written instructions.

question: Under REEB 24.13(3)(a), when presenting written proposals to a client, a licensee must:
choice_a: Recommend only the proposal that offers the licensee the highest commission
choice_b: Present only proposals that meet or exceed the listing price
choice_c: Wait until all proposals are received before presenting any of them
choice_d: Present each proposal objectively and inform the client of both its advantages and its disadvantages
explanation: REEB 24.13(3)(a) requires licensees to present written proposals to clients in an objective and fair manner, disclosing both the advantages and the disadvantages of each.

question: If a seller has already received one written offer, may a listing licensee withhold a second written offer received later from another buyer until the seller has acted on the first offer?
choice_a: No; under REEB 24.13(3)(c), licensees must promptly present all written proposals to the client and may not withhold a proposal pending action on a prior one, absent contrary written client instructions
choice_b: Yes, offers must always be presented strictly in the order received
choice_c: Yes, if the second offer is for a lower price
choice_d: Yes, if the second buyer is represented by the same firm as the first buyer
explanation: REEB 24.13(3)(c) requires licensees to promptly present all proposals to their client and prohibits withholding a proposal pending action on a prior offer, absent contrary written instructions from the client.

question: Under Wis. Stat. § 452.132(2), what must a real estate firm do regarding the board's rules on licensee conduct and ethical practices?
choice_a: Post a hard copy of the entire Wisconsin Administrative Code in the firm's lobby
choice_b: Notify each licensee associated with the firm where a copy of the board's rules relating to conduct, ethical practices, and licensee responsibilities may be obtained
choice_c: Mail a printed copy of Chapter 452 to every client at the start of each transaction
choice_d: Require licensees to pass an annual internal ethics exam administered by the firm
explanation: Wis. Stat. § 452.132(2) requires a firm to provide licensees with written operating procedures and to notify each associated licensee where a copy of the board's rules on conduct, ethics, and licensee responsibilities may be obtained.

question: Under REEB 24.17(1), within how many hours must a licensee notify the board after being convicted of a crime?
choice_a: 7 calendar days
choice_b: 30 days
choice_c: 48 hours, along with documentation of the conviction
choice_d: There is no notification requirement unless the board specifically asks
explanation: REEB 24.17(1) requires a licensee convicted of a crime to notify the board within 48 hours, with documentation, so the board can determine whether the crime substantially relates to real estate practice under Wis. Stat. § 111.335(3)(a).

question: What does REEB 24.17(4) prohibit?
choice_a: Taking a scheduled vacation during an active listing period
choice_b: Referring a transaction to another licensee within the same firm
choice_c: Working more than 40 hours in a given week
choice_d: Providing real estate services while the licensee's ability to competently perform their duties is impaired by a mental or emotional disorder, drugs, or alcohol
explanation: REEB 24.17(4) prohibits a licensee from providing real estate services while their ability to competently perform their duties is impaired by a mental or emotional disorder, drugs, or alcohol.

question: Under REEB 24.17(5), within how many days must a licensee or applicant respond to a request for information from the department or board?
choice_a: 30 days from the date of the request
choice_b: 5 business days
choice_c: 10 calendar days
choice_d: 90 days
explanation: REEB 24.17(5) requires licensees and applicants to respond to department and board requests for information within 30 days of the date of the request.

question: Under REEB 24.085, what is prohibited?
choice_a: Preparing a standard form purchase contract on behalf of a client
choice_b: Drafting or using any document that the licensee knows falsely portrays an interest in real estate
choice_c: Listing a property that the licensee personally owns, if properly disclosed
choice_d: Using a fill-in-the-blank template offer to purchase form
explanation: REEB 24.085 prohibits a licensee from drafting or using any document the licensee knows falsely portrays an interest in real estate.

question: Under REEB 24.06(2), how must a licensee treat a party's desire to consult an attorney about a transaction?
choice_a: The licensee should discourage it to avoid delaying the transaction
choice_b: The licensee may charge an additional fee if an attorney becomes involved
choice_c: The licensee must not discourage any person from retaining an attorney
choice_d: The licensee must require attorney review on every transaction
explanation: REEB 24.06(2) provides that licensees shall not discourage any person from retaining an attorney.

question: Under REEB 24.15, the prohibition on issuing checks with insufficient funds applies to checks drawn on which accounts?
choice_a: Only a licensee's personal checking account
choice_b: Only checks issued to the Wisconsin Department of Revenue
choice_c: Only checks exceeding $10,000
choice_d: A licensee's business or trust accounts
explanation: REEB 24.15 prohibits licensees from issuing checks upon business or trust accounts that contain insufficient funds.

question: Under REEB 24.02(3), how is "brokerage service" defined?
choice_a: Any service described under Wis. Stat. § 452.01(2) that is provided to a person by a firm and any licensees associated with the firm
choice_b: Any service provided exclusively by a licensed appraiser
choice_c: Only services related to residential leasing
choice_d: Any service provided by an unlicensed personal assistant
explanation: REEB 24.02(3) defines "brokerage service" as any service described under s. 452.01(2), Stats., provided to a person by a firm and any licensees associated with the firm.

question: Under REEB 24.02(4), how is "builder" defined for purposes of the tie-in arrangement rules?
choice_a: Only a corporation licensed as a general contractor by the state
choice_b: Any person engaged in the business of constructing homes without a buyer under contract or constructing homes under a contract with the buyer
choice_c: A person who exclusively remodels existing homes
choice_d: A licensee who occasionally performs handyman work
explanation: REEB 24.02(4) defines "builder" as any person engaged in the business of constructing homes without a buyer under contract or constructing homes under a contract with the buyer, a definition relevant to the REEB 24.075 tie-in arrangement exceptions.

question: Under REEB 24.02(10), "effectively controlled" means having the power or authority to cause the transfer of an interest in real estate, but this definition specifically excludes what?
choice_a: Ownership of the property in fee simple
choice_b: A power of attorney granted by the owner
choice_c: The authority conferred by a real estate listing contract
choice_d: A recorded easement across the property
explanation: REEB 24.02(10) defines "effectively controlled" as having the power or authority to cause the transfer of an interest in real estate for oneself or another, but does not include the authority conferred by a real estate listing contract; this distinction matters because REEB 24.075 applies the tie-in prohibitions to real estate a licensee owns or effectively controls.

question: Under REEB 24.02(18), which of the following falls within the definition of "transaction"?
choice_a: Only transactions that close within the same calendar year they were listed
choice_b: Only transactions involving licensed appraisers
choice_c: Only transactions where both parties are represented by attorneys
choice_d: The sale, exchange, purchase, or rental of, or the granting or acceptance of an option to sell, exchange, purchase, or rent, an interest in real estate, a business, or a business opportunity
explanation: REEB 24.02(18) broadly defines "transaction" to include the sale, exchange, purchase, or rental of, or the granting or acceptance of an option regarding, an interest in real estate, a business, or a business opportunity.

question: Under REEB 24.03(2)(b), licensees have an affirmative obligation to do what?
choice_a: Act to protect the public against fraud, misrepresentation, and unethical practices
choice_b: Guarantee the accuracy of every statement made by a seller
choice_c: Personally investigate the criminal history of all transaction parties
choice_d: Refuse to work with unrepresented buyers
explanation: REEB 24.03(2)(b) requires licensees to act to protect the public against fraud, misrepresentation, and unethical practices.

question: Under REEB 24.03(2)(c), a licensee shall be knowledgeable regarding which of the following, and assist, guide, and advise the parties accordingly?
choice_a: Federal income tax preparation requirements
choice_b: Laws, public policies, and current market conditions on real estate matters
choice_c: Structural engineering standards for high-rise construction
choice_d: Title insurance underwriting formulas
explanation: REEB 24.03(2)(c) requires a licensee to be knowledgeable regarding laws, public policies, and current market conditions on real estate matters, and to assist, guide, and advise the parties on these factors.

question: Under Wis. Stat. § 452.136(2)(b), how must a licensee associated with a firm advertise (apart from advertising the licensee's own rental property)?
choice_a: Under the licensee's own name exclusively, without reference to the firm
choice_b: Using only the firm's logo, without any name required
choice_c: Under the supervision of, and in the name of, the firm, with the firm's name displayed clearly and conspicuously
choice_d: Under the name of the licensee's spouse if the spouse is also licensed
explanation: Wis. Stat. § 452.136(2)(b) requires a licensee associated with a firm to advertise under the supervision of and in the name of the firm, with the firm's name displayed clearly and conspicuously, subject to limited exceptions for rental of licensee-owned property and independent practice under s. 452.30(6).

question: Under Wis. Stat. § 452.136(2)(c), a licensee advertising the occasional sale of real estate the licensee personally owns, without complying with the firm-name disclosure requirements, must do what instead?
choice_a: Obtain board pre-approval for the advertisement
choice_b: List the property exclusively through the licensee's own firm
choice_c: Disclose the exact commission the licensee would have earned on a comparable listing
choice_d: Clearly identify himself, herself, or itself as a real estate licensee in the advertisement
explanation: Wis. Stat. § 452.136(2)(c) allows a licensee to advertise the occasional sale of licensee-owned real estate without complying with the firm-name disclosure rules, provided the licensee clearly identifies himself, herself, or itself as a real estate licensee in the advertisement.

question: Under REEB 24.05(1), a licensee's compensation practices must follow the requirements specified in which statutory provision?
choice_a: Wis. Stat. § 452.133(3)(a) and (c)
choice_b: Wis. Stat. § 452.137
choice_c: Wis. Stat. § 452.20
choice_d: Wis. Stat. § 452.42
explanation: REEB 24.05(1) incorporates the compensation-related prohibited conduct rules in Wis. Stat. § 452.133(3)(a) (restricting fees from persons other than the client or firm absent written consent) and (c) (referral compensation disclosure).
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 24.05(1); Wis. Stat. § 452.133(3)(a), (c)

question: Under REEB 24.05(2), a licensee's "disclosure of interest" obligations are governed by which statutory provision?
choice_a: Wis. Stat. § 452.19(1m)
explanation: REEB 24.05(2) requires licensees to follow the disclosure-of-interest requirements in Wis. Stat. § 452.133(3)(b), which bars a licensee from acting in a transaction on the licensee's own behalf, on behalf of immediate family, the licensee's firm, or an entity in which the licensee has an interest, without the prior written consent of all parties.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 24.05(2); Wis. Stat. § 452.133(3)(b)

question: What does REEB 24.06(1) prohibit?
choice_a: Licensees referring clients to attorneys for closing services
choice_b: Licensees explaining the general provisions of a board-approved form
choice_c: Licensees engaging in activities that constitute the unauthorized practice of law
choice_d: Licensees recommending a title company to a buyer
explanation: REEB 24.06(1) provides that licensees shall not engage in activities that constitute the unauthorized practice of law.

question: Under REEB 24.07(1)(a), what must a licensee do when engaging in real estate practice involving vacant land that is accessible?
choice_a: Obtain a licensed surveyor's plat before listing the parcel
choice_b: Test the soil for contamination at the licensee's own expense
choice_c: Inspect the land only if specifically requested by the buyer
choice_d: Conduct a reasonably competent and diligent inspection of the vacant land to detect observable material adverse facts
explanation: REEB 24.07(1)(a) requires that, if vacant land is accessible, a licensee conduct a reasonably competent and diligent inspection of the vacant land to detect observable material adverse facts.

question: Under REEB 24.07(1)(c), when must a licensee OTHER than the listing licensee (such as a buyer's agent) inspect the real estate?
choice_a: Prior to submitting a written proposal, unless the licensee is denied access or instructed to submit the proposal first, in which case inspection must occur promptly after submission once access is given
choice_b: Only after the offer to purchase has been fully accepted
choice_c: Within 90 days after closing
choice_d: There is no inspection obligation for any licensee other than the listing licensee
explanation: REEB 24.07(1)(c) requires licensees other than the listing licensee to inspect the real estate prior to submitting a written proposal, unless denied access or instructed by a party to submit the proposal first, in which case the inspection must occur promptly after submission once access is given.

question: Under REEB 24.07(4), if a licensee becomes aware that a party has not disclosed that party's entire agreement regarding the transaction to that party's secured lender, what must the licensee do?
choice_a: Report the omission only to the board
choice_b: Disclose this fact, in writing and in a timely manner, to the party's secured lender
choice_c: Do nothing, since lender disclosures are solely the party's responsibility
choice_d: Disclose the omission verbally to the other party in the transaction
explanation: REEB 24.07(4) requires a licensee who becomes aware that a party has not disclosed their entire agreement regarding a transaction to that party's secured lender to disclose this fact, in writing and in a timely manner, to the secured lender.

question: Under REEB 24.07(5), a licensee may rely on the results of a qualified third party's inspection or investigation only if the licensee does what?
choice_a: Personally re-performs the same inspection
choice_b: Obtains the third party's professional liability insurance certificate
choice_c: Obtains a written report of the inspection or investigation and delivers a copy to all parties in a timely manner
choice_d: Keeps the report confidential unless a party specifically requests it
explanation: REEB 24.07(5) permits a licensee to rely on a qualified third party's inspection or investigation results only if the licensee obtains a written report and delivers a copy of that report to all parties in a timely manner.

question: Under REEB 24.07(8)(a)1r, when a firm is negotiating on behalf of a party who is not its client and the transaction involves residential real estate with one to four dwelling units, what must the firm additionally request?
choice_a: A notarized statement of the party's net worth
choice_b: The party's written waiver of all statutory duties
choice_c: A background check authorization from the party
choice_d: The party's signed acknowledgement that the party has received a copy of the written disclosure statement
explanation: REEB 24.07(8)(a)1r requires a firm negotiating for a non-client party on residential property with one to four dwelling units to request the party's signed acknowledgement of receipt of the written disclosure statement required under Wis. Stat. § 452.135.

question: Under REEB 24.07(8)(a)2, a licensee representing a buyer of one-to-four-family residential property who is negotiating directly with the seller must notify the seller of the buyer agency relationship at the earliest of which events?
choice_a: The first contact exchanging information, a showing of the property, or any other negotiation with the seller or listing firm
choice_b: Only at the time the offer to purchase is signed
choice_c: Only if the seller specifically asks who represents the buyer
choice_d: Within 5 business days after the buyer signs a buyer agency agreement
explanation: REEB 24.07(8)(a)2 requires a buyer's agent negotiating directly with the seller of 1-4 family residential property to notify the seller or listing firm of the buyer agency relationship at the earliest of first contact exchanging information, a showing, or any other negotiation.

question: Under REEB 24.07(8)(b)2, when may a firm permit another firm to act as a subagent in a transaction?
choice_a: Any time the firm believes it would benefit the transaction
choice_b: Only if the firm's client has authorized the use of a subagent in the agency agreement
choice_c: Only after the property has been on the market for 30 days
choice_d: Subagency is categorically prohibited under Wisconsin law
explanation: REEB 24.07(8)(b)2 prohibits a firm or its licensees from permitting other firms to act as subagents in a transaction unless the firm's client has authorized the use of a subagent in the agency agreement.

question: Under REEB 24.07(8)(c), what must a licensee state in an offer to purchase, lease, option to purchase, or exchange agreement?
choice_a: The exact square footage of the property
choice_b: The licensee's continuing education credit hours
choice_c: Whom the licensee represents as an agent in the transaction
choice_d: The names of all prior owners of the property
explanation: REEB 24.07(8)(c) requires licensees to state, in the offer to purchase, lease, option to purchase, or exchange agreement, whom the licensee represents as an agent in the transaction.

question: Under REEB 24.075(3)(a), a licensee may condition the sale of vacant land on the buyer's using a specific builder if which condition is met?
choice_a: The builder is the buyer's relative
choice_b: The builder submitted the lowest bid among competing builders
choice_c: The buyer has not yet obtained financing
choice_d: The builder owns a bona fide interest in the real estate, and there is full disclosure as specified under Wis. Stat. § 452.133(3)(c)
explanation: REEB 24.075(3)(a) recognizes an exception to the vacant-land builder tie-in prohibition where the builder owns a bona fide interest in the real estate and there is full disclosure as specified under Wis. Stat. § 452.133(3)(c).

question: Under REEB 24.075(3)(c), a tie-in requiring a buyer of vacant land to use a specific builder is permitted when the agreement:
choice_a: Is a bona fide effort to maintain development quality or architectural uniformity, and no consideration passes from a builder to a licensee for soliciting the agreement
choice_b: Was requested by the seller's attorney
choice_c: Only affects lots larger than five acres
choice_d: Is limited to a single builder chosen by the licensee's firm
explanation: REEB 24.075(3)(c) permits a builder tie-in requirement on vacant land when the agreement is a bona fide effort to maintain development quality or architectural uniformity and no consideration passes from a builder to a licensee for soliciting the agreement.

question: Under REEB 24.13(3)(b), if a firm has a property listed, when is a licensee associated with that firm prohibited from submitting a personal written proposal to purchase the property?
choice_a: At any time, with no exceptions whatsoever
choice_b: If the licensee has knowledge of the terms of any pending offer, except that the firm may arrange for a guaranteed sale at the time of listing
choice_c: Only during the final 10 days before closing
choice_d: Only if the licensee personally is the listing agent, not any other agent at the firm
explanation: REEB 24.13(3)(b) prohibits a licensee associated with the listing firm from submitting a personal written proposal or offer to purchase the listed property if the licensee has knowledge of the terms of any pending offer, except that the firm may arrange for a guaranteed sale at the time of listing.

question: Under REEB 24.13(4), when a written statement of the date and time a proposal was presented, rejected, or expired is requested by the other party's firm, what must a licensee do?
choice_a: Provide the statement only if the request itself is made in writing
choice_b: Provide the statement within 30 days of the request
choice_c: Immediately provide the written statement to the other party's firm
choice_d: Decline, since presentation timing is confidential
explanation: REEB 24.13(4) requires a licensee to immediately provide a written statement including the date and time a proposal was presented, or rejected or expired without acceptance, to the other party's firm when such a statement is requested.

question: Under REEB 24.13(5), if a licensee knows that a party has an unexpired written contract granting another licensee an exclusive right to sell, lease, or negotiate, with whom must all negotiations be conducted?
choice_a: Directly with the party at all times, regardless of the exclusive contract
choice_b: Only through the Real Estate Examining Board
choice_c: Only through the party's attorney
choice_d: The firm holding the exclusive right to sell, lease, or negotiate, not directly with the party, except with that firm's consent or in similarly compelling circumstances
explanation: REEB 24.13(5) requires that negotiations be conducted with the firm holding an exclusive right to sell, lease, or negotiate, and not directly with the party, except with the firm's consent or where the absence of the firm or similar circumstances reasonably compels direct negotiation.

question: Under REEB 24.17(2), what serves as presumptive evidence of a licensee's conviction of a crime for board discipline purposes?
choice_a: A certified copy of a judgment of a court of record showing the conviction, whether within Wisconsin or elsewhere
choice_b: A newspaper article reporting the conviction
choice_c: An unsworn statement from the licensee's employer
choice_d: The licensee's own verbal admission alone, without documentation
explanation: REEB 24.17(2) provides that a certified copy of a judgment of a court of record showing a conviction, within this state or without, is presumptive evidence of the conviction for purposes of board discipline.

question: Under REEB 24.17(2m), the board may revoke a license based on what?
choice_a: Any misdemeanor traffic citation
choice_b: A conviction of a felony that is a bar to licensure under Wis. Stat. § 452.25(1)(a)
choice_c: A civil judgment unrelated to real estate practice
choice_d: A single instance of a licensee returning a call to the board late
explanation: REEB 24.17(2m) authorizes the board to revoke a license based on a conviction of a felony that is a bar to licensure under Wis. Stat. § 452.25(1)(a).

question: Under REEB 24.17(3), licensees may not violate, or aid or abet the violation of, which of the following?
choice_a: Only rules specific to their own license type (broker versus salesperson)
choice_b: Only local municipal zoning ordinances
choice_c: Ch. 452, Stats., chs. REEB 11 to 25, or any order of the board
choice_d: Federal securities law
explanation: REEB 24.17(3) prohibits licensees from violating, or aiding or abetting the violation of, any provisions or terms or conditions of ch. 452, Stats., chs. REEB 11 to 25, or any order of the board.

question: Under Wis. Stat. § 452.132(1)(b), a firm must provide a licensee with what regarding a supervising broker?
choice_a: A guaranteed minimum number of hours of direct supervision each week
choice_b: A written performance review every 90 days
choice_c: A dedicated office space within the same building as the supervising broker
choice_d: Reasonable access to a supervising broker for the purpose of consultation regarding real estate practice issues
explanation: Wis. Stat. § 452.132(1)(b) requires a firm to provide a licensee with reasonable access to a supervising broker for the purpose of consultation regarding real estate practice issues.

question: Under Wis. Stat. § 452.132(2)(a), a firm must provide each associated licensee with what?
choice_a: A written statement of the procedures under which the firm and its licensees must operate with respect to handling leases, agency agreements, offers to purchase, and other transaction documents and records
choice_b: A copy of the firm's annual financial statements
choice_c: A list of every other licensee's commission split
choice_d: A signed non-compete agreement
explanation: Wis. Stat. § 452.132(2)(a) requires a firm to provide each licensee associated with the firm a written statement of the procedures for handling leases, agency agreements, offers to purchase, and other documents and records relating to transactions.

question: Under Wis. Stat. § 452.132(2)(c), a firm must ensure that a licensee holds a valid license at which points in time?
choice_a: Only at the time the licensee is first hired, with no ongoing obligation
choice_b: Before the licensee becomes associated with the firm, and at the beginning of each biennial licensure period
choice_c: Only when a consumer complaint is filed against the licensee
choice_d: Only upon the licensee's own request
explanation: Wis. Stat. § 452.132(2)(c) requires a firm to ensure, before a licensee becomes associated with the firm and at the beginning of each biennial licensure period, that the licensee holds a valid license.
